 JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner is as follows: That on 15022021 at about 0700 p.m., the petitioner was riding the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA 09EB1559 along with his friend Abhishek as pillion rider towards their working place at Narayanapura and after completion of their work when they were proceeding towards Hosahalli village and when they reached near Narayanapura Melukote road at that time the rider of the Passion Pro motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA54E3505 came with opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the vehicle of the petitioner, result of which the petitioner and pillion rider fell down and petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately he was shifted to Government Hospital, Pandavapura wherein first aid treatment was given and then he was shifted to K.R Hospital, Mysore and thereafter with the advise of the duty doctor, he was shifted to S.T Jonh's Medical College Hospital wherein admitted as an inpatient from 16022021 to 2602202.
He undergone the treatment of plastic surgery.
Thereafter he was discharged with advice to take follow up treatment as outpatient.
So far the petitioner has spent a sum of Rs.5,00,000/ towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges etc.,
Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy.
He was aged about 23 years, he was working as Auto driver and thereby earning sum of Rs.20,000/ p.m.
Due to the permanent disability petitioner is not in a position to do the said work.
He has suffered pain and sufferings, permanent disability, loss of income, loss of future income and other pecuniary and non pecuniary damages.
3. The RC owner of the Passion Pro motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA54E3505 (herein after referred to as offending vehicle) was died leaving behind respondent no.1 to 3 as his Lrs.
The 4th respondent is the rider of the offending vehicle.

4. In response to the issuance of notice, the Respondents did not appear, hence they were placed ex parte.
5.

On the basis of the above pleadings the following points are framed:
POINT

sentences.text:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that he met with a Road Traffic accident on 1502 2021 at about 700 P.m., on Melukote Chinakurali road, near the proprety belongs to Swamygowda S/o Dyavegowda and sustained grievous injuries due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of Hero Honda Passion Pro motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA54E3505?
2. Whether the petitioner proves that he is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3. What Order or Award?
6. The petitioner got examined himself as Pw1 and marked Ex.P1 to Ex.P11 and closed evidence on his side.
The respondents neither have chosen to conduct the cross examination of Pw.1 nor led their evidence.

7. Heard arguments of learned counsel for the petitioner and perused the entire materials placed on record.
8.

My findings on the above points are as follows:
Point No.1: In the Affirmative Point No.2: Partly in the affirmative.

Point No.3: As per final order, for the following;
REASONS 9. POINT No.1 :

In order to explain the actionable negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle,
P.W.1 has filed his affidavit explaining the vivid picture of the accident that took place on 1502 2021 at about 0700 p.m., when he was riding his motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA09EB1559 along with pillion rider on Melukote Chinakurali road, near the property belongs to Swamygowda,
S/o Dyavegowda, at that time the rider of the offending vehicle came from opposite direction in rash and negligent manner and dashed against his motorcycle and caused the accident.

P.W.1 further deposed about the nature of injuries sustained, treatment taken and the amount spent for treatment etc.
10.

In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent riding by the rider of offending vehicle, P.W.1 has relied upon Ex.P1 to 7 which are the police records such as FIR, spot mahazar,
seizer mahazar, wound certificate, charge sheet, IMV report, MLC record, etc.
11.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by the Narashimegowda, case has been registered against the rider of the offending vehicle in Crime No 0068/2021 of Pandavapura PS for the offence punishable under section 279, 337 IPC.
The Investigation officer after investigation filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Section 279, 337,338 IPC and u/Sec.181(3), 196 MV Act.

sentences.text: If the spot mahazar is perused, the width of the road at the spot of accident is nearly 16 feet.
The petitioner was proceeding from Narayanapura towards Hosahalli.
The offending vehicle was coming from opposite direction.
It is two way road.
The spot of accident is at a distance of nearly 2 feet from left edge of Narayanapura Hosahalli tar road towards right side.
It means, the rider of offending vehicle by taking his vehicle on the extreme right side of Hosahalli Narayanapura road hit against the vehicle of the petitioner.
Had the rider of the offending vehicle ridden his vehicle on the left side of Hosahalli - Narayanapura road this accident would not have occurred.
Further respondents have not disputed the involvement of offending vehicle so also the manner of accident one stated by the petitioner.
Hence, negligence can be solely attributed against the respondent no.4 who is the rider of the offending vehicle.
Accordingly, I answer Point No.1 is in the affirmative.
13. POINT No.2:
In view of my finding on issue no.1 that the petitioner has sustained injuries as a direct result of the accident, he is entitled to claim compensation.
The petitioner has given evidence to the effect of his sustained injures over his body.

Ex.P4 is the wound certificate issued from ST.
John's Medical College Hospital, Bangalore, to the effect that the petitioner has been treated for five injuries of which four injuries are grievous in nature and one is simple in nature.
14.

entities.text:
ST.
John's Medical College Hospital, Bangalore
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The case summary & discharge summary as per Ex.P.10 issued from ST.Jonh's Medical College Hospital, discloses that petitioner has taken treatment from 1502 2021 to 26022021 for a period of 12 days and underwent Arch bar+ORIF for ZygomaticoMaxillary buttress fracture, Naso Maxillary buttress fracture, ORIF +K wire fixation for first metacarpal base fracture along with fixation with miniplates (synthes) +debridement & tacking suturing for left index finger tip near total amputation injury was done under GA on 22022021.

The petitioner has not examined the medical officer who has given treatment to him and no evidence on record to say that he has suffered permanent disability and because of permanent disability there is loss of future income.
Hence, petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head of loss of future income.
15. Towards pain and sufferings, the petitioner shown to have sustained four grievous injuries.

Hence taking in to consideration the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment etc it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.75,000/ towards pain and suffering.
16. So far as medical expenses incurred by the petitioner is concerned, he has produced medical bills and inpatient medical bills for sum of Rs.1,14,734/ at Ex.P.8 and 9.
Hence, petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,14,734/ under the head medical expenses.

17. Further for 12 days of hospitalization at ST.John's Medical College Hospital, Bengaluru and for his taking follow up treatment in the said hospitals, requires an attendant, was traveled to hospital for treatment, for followups has incurred traveling expenses, he has taken nourishment and need further nourishment at this age and incurred other incidental expenses therefore all together incidental expenses is assessed at Rs.30,000/.
18.
It is submitted by petitioner that he was working as Auto driver and thereby earning sum of Rs.20,000/ per month.

But to substantiate the said contention petitioner has not produced any Praveen H.N. Alias Praveen Kumar H.N vs Lakshmamma on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52190834/
4 materials.

sentences.text:
Hence this court considering the age of the petitioner, the year of accident and place of residence of the petitioner considers the income of the petitioner as Rs.15,000/ p.m.
19.
The petitioner has sustained four grievous injuries and taken treatment for 12 days as inpatient.
Hence the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner which are grievous in nature it is reasonable to hold that period of three month as complete laid down period.
Hence taking in to consideration the avocation of the petitioner and loss of income caused from said avocation this court takes the loss of income during laid down period for 3 month.
Hence petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.45,000/ towards loss of income during the laid down period.
20. The petitioner at his age of 23 years has suffered grievous injuries.
Hence taking in to consideration the said aspect the petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.30,000/ towards loss of amenities and discomforts.

Sl. Heads Amount No.
1.
Towards pain and sufferings Rs. 75,000/

2. Towards Conveyance, Attendant Rs. 30,000/
 charges and nourishing food 3.

Medical expenses Rs. 1,14,734/
4. Loss of income during laid down Rs. 45,000/
 period 5.
Loss of discomfort and amenities Rs. 30,000/
Total Rs.2,94,734/

Therefore this court holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.2,94,734/ ( Rupees Two Lakh Ninety Four Thousand Seven Hundred Thirty Four only).
21.

As per the discussion made above, the respondents remained absent and have not led any evidence and therefore, as there is no insurance policy, the RC owner of the offending motorcycle was died leaving behind his Lr's respondent nos.1 to 3 and the respondent no.4 is rider of the said offending vehicle.
The respondent no.1 to 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
The compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6 % per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
In the result Point No.2 is answered partly in the Affirmative.
22. POINT No.3: In the light of findings given on Point No.1 and 2, my finding on this point is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.2,94,734/ ( Rupees Two Lakh Ninety Four Thousand Seven Hundred Thirty Four only) with interest at 6 % p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
